sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case asks when a person may sue for an illegal search. One side argues the right to sue begins immediately upon the violation. The other side argues the right to sue waits until the criminal conviction is overturned.

paragraphs: The Supreme Court heard oral argument in this case on November 6, 2006.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the side that brought the case wants to sue immediately after the illegal search occurs.
the opposing side wants the lawsuit to wait until the criminal conviction is invalidated.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the start of the clock for suing over illegal searches. It determines how long citizens wait to seek redress. It shapes the balance between criminal proceedings and civil rights claims.
